methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json), cross-checked against research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json and body-page OCR (derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/) per the documented source-recovery protocol. Dermatology's TOC page (pdf 189) is a two-column layout whose OCR interleaved adjacent-column text onto single lines; the majority of the chapter's 42 toc_inventory.json nodes therefore carry titles that concatenate two unrelated real headings (documented individually in same_page_merge_resolutions below), and 7 real headings received no node at all (documented in unresolved_heading_resolution below, resolved here via body-heading confirmation and assigned synthetic UNCATALOGUED: ids per the documented convention). Generic structural/umbrella headings with no independent content beyond their already-covered children are NOT converted into standalone units - see organizational_header_nodes below.

unresolved_heading_resolution: research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json records 7 entries for chapter_code D, all resulting from the same TOC-page (pdf 189) two-column-OCR page-number-parsing failure. All 7 were resolved via body-heading confirmation (steps 1-3 of the source-recovery protocol: raw OCR of derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/, normalized text in derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/, and direct body-page heading confirmation) rather than left unresolved, since each heading's real body-page content was locatable and unambiguous: 'Introductionto Skin' and 'Morphology' -> SU-D-02/SU-D-03 (assigned UNCATALOGUED:D-intro-skin and UNCATALOGUED:D-morphology-approach); 'Patterns and Distribution' -> folded into SU-D-03; 'Differential Diagnoses for Common Presentations' -> folded into SU-D-03; 'Common SkinLesions' -> no standalone unit needed, all of its child subsections (Cysts, Fibrous Lesions, Hyperkeratotic Lesions, Keloids, Pigmented Lesions, Vascular Lesions) are already accounted for via their own merged nodes (SU-D-04 through SU-D-08); 'AcneiformEruptions' -> no standalone unit needed, fully accounted for via D.S08/D.S08.T01 (SU-D-09/SU-D-10); 'Papulosquamous Diseases' -> SU-D-13/SU-D-14 (assigned UNCATALOGUED:D-papulosquamous-lp-pr and UNCATALOGUED:D-psoriasis). Two further headings with real body-page content but no toc_inventory.json node AND no entry in unresolved_headings.json (i.e., silently dropped by the extraction pass rather than flagged) were independently found via full body-page reading of pdf 189-246 and are resolved the same way: 'Pre-Malignant Skin Conditions' -> SU-D-34 (UNCATALOGUED:D-premalignant); 'Sunscreens and Preventative Therapy' -> SU-D-45 (UNCATALOGUED:D-sunscreens); 'Dermatologic Therapies' -> SU-D-46 (UNCATALOGUED:D-derm-therapies); 'Landmark Dermatology Trials' -> SU-D-48 (UNCATALOGUED:D-trials).

study_units.title: Skin Anatomy, Function, and Age-Related Changes
source_hierarchy_path: UNCATALOGUED:D-intro-skin (Introduction to Skin: Normal Processes of Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue)
study_units.structural_rationale: The TOC heading 'Introduction to Skin' (raw OCR 'Introductionto Skin') has no corresponding node in toc_inventory.json: research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json records it as UNRESOLVED because its trailing TOC page-number digits did not parse to a trustworthy page anchor. Body-heading confirmation (clean-ocr/0190.txt-0192.txt, pdf 190-192) locates the real content directly: page D2 closes the acronym table and transitions into aging-related skin change content; page D3 (pdf 191) carries the confirmed body subheading 'Skin Anatomy' (epidermal/dermal layers, cells, epidermal appendages) preceded by unheaded content on senile purpura/aging; page D4 (pdf 192) opens with 'Cutaneous Glands' and 'Skin Function' before the confirmed 'Morphology' heading begins later on the same page. Assigned synthetic id UNCATALOGUED:D-intro-skin per the documented same-page-merge/unresolved-heading convention (no toc_inventory.json node exists for this heading or its content).

study_units.title: Approach to Skin Lesions: Morphology, Distribution, and Differential Diagnosis of Common Presentations
source_hierarchy_path: UNCATALOGUED:D-morphology-approach (Morphology; Patterns and Distribution; Differential Diagnoses for Common Presentations)
study_units.structural_rationale: Three TOC headings ('Morphology', 'Patterns and Distribution' [merged on its raw TOC line with 'Pre-Malignant Skin Conditions'], 'Differential Diagnoses for Common Presentations') are each recorded UNRESOLVED in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json with no toc_inventory.json node. Body-heading confirmation (clean-ocr/0192.txt-0196.txt, pdf 192-196) confirms all three as real, contiguous body headings: 'Morphology' with 'Primary Lesions'/'Secondary Lesions' subheadings and the SCALDA lesion-description mnemonic (pdf 192-194); 'Patterns and Distribution' with Table 2 of pattern/distribution terms (pdf 195); 'Differential Diagnoses for Common Presentations' with Table 3, a DDx-by-lesion-morphology table (pdf 195-196). Combined into one study unit as a single clinical-reasoning skill (describing and localizing a lesion to generate a differential) rather than three separate diagnoses, consistent with the instruction not to fragment a shared approach/skill into artificial sub-units. Assigned synthetic id UNCATALOGUED:D-morphology-approach.

Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0196.txt) shows Table 4 'Cysts' (Epidermal Cyst, Pilar Cyst, Dermoid Cyst, Milium) directly under the 'Common Skin Lesions' heading on pdf 196. D.S06.T02 (garbled 'Hyperkeratotic Lesions Malignant Melanoma' - 'Hyperkeratotic Lesions' fragment)
study_units.structural_rationale: Each of these three T-children is a two-column TOC merge pairing a 'Common Skin Lesions' subsection with an unrelated 'Malignant Skin Tumours' subsection. Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0197.txt-0198.txt, pdf 197-198) shows the real, contiguous content: 'Fibrous Lesions' (Dermatofibroma, Skin Tags), 'Hyperkeratotic Lesions' (Seborrheic Keratosis; cross-refs to Actinic Keratosis/Keratoacanthoma covered elsewhere; Corns), and 'Keloids' - three short, clinically related benign-growth topics grouped into one study unit per the instruction to combine generic/short subheadings rather than fragment them individually. source_hierarchy_path: D.S06.T04 (Pigmented Lesions - not merged; a complete standalone TOC fragment)

study_units.title: Atopic Dermatitis
source_hierarchy_path: D.S02 (garbled title 'Dermatitis' - real heading 'Dermatitis (Eczema)'; this unit represents its Atopic Dermatitis subsection)

study_units.structural_rationale: The TOC heading 'Papulosquamous Diseases' is recorded UNRESOLVED in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json (its raw OCR line pairs it with the distant, unrelated 'Sunscreens and Preventative Therapy' heading, confirming a two-column TOC merge with no page-number anchor for either fragment). Body-heading confirmation (clean-ocr/0208.txt, pdf 208) confirms 'Papulosquamous Diseases' as a real heading immediately followed by 'Lichen Planus' and 'Pityriasis Rosea' subheadings, both fully contained on pdf 208. Psoriasis, the third and much larger subtype under this same umbrella heading, is split into its own unit (SU-D-14) given its substantially deeper content (4 pages, multiple tables, biologics). Assigned synthetic id UNCATALOGUED:D-papulosquamous-lp-pr; the 'Sunscreens and Preventative Therapy' fragment sharing this TOC line is represented separately (SU-D-45).

study_units.title: Psoriasis (Plaque, Guttate, Erythrodermic, Pustular, Inverse) and Systemic Therapy
study_units.structural_rationale: Continuation of the 'Papulosquamous Diseases' umbrella heading documented in SU-D-13 (UNRESOLVED in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json). Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0208.txt-0211.txt, pdf 208-211) shows Psoriasis as the largest subsection: classification, pathophysiology, epidemiology, plaque psoriasis, Table 14/15 topical and systemic treatment, Table 16 biologics approved in Canada, guttate/erythrodermic/pustular/inverse subtypes, and psoriatic arthritis (split separately, SU-D-15, as a distinct cross-discipline topic). Split from SU-D-13 given its markedly greater depth. Assigned synthetic id UNCATALOGUED:D-psoriasis.

study_units.title: Psoriatic Arthritis (cross-reference to Rheumatology)
source_hierarchy_path: UNCATALOGUED:D-psoriasis (Psoriatic Arthritis subsection, cross-referenced to Rheumatology RH25)
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0211.txt, pdf 211): a brief standalone paragraph noting psoriatic arthritis prevalence among psoriasis patients and an explicit 'see Rheumatology, RH25' cross-reference, with no independent dermatology-specific content beyond the epidemiologic link (nail/scalp involvement as a risk marker). Represented as its own unit (rather than folded into SU-D-14) because it is a distinct joint-disease presentation outside the dermatologic scope of this chapter.

study_units.title: Bullous Pemphigoid
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0211.txt, pdf 211) confirms 'Vesiculobullous Diseases' as an unmerged heading immediately followed by 'Bullous Pemphigoid' as its first subsection (clinical features, IgG-BP180/BP230 pathophysiology, immunofluorescence findings, prednisone-based management).

study_units.title: Pemphigus Vulgaris and Pemphigus Foliaceus
study_units.structural_rationale: D.S15's title concatenates the real heading 'Pemphigus Vulgaris' (continuation of the Vesiculobullous Diseases section, pdf 211-212) with the unrelated 'References' bibliography heading at D58 (pdf 246) via a shared TOC line. Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0211.txt-0212.txt) shows Pemphigus Vulgaris (Nikolsky/Asboe-Hansen signs, anti-desmoglein IgG, immunosuppressive management) followed by a Pemphigus Foliaceus sidebar. The 'References' fragment of this node_id is represented separately (SU-D-48, folded with Landmark Trials as non-testable bibliographic content).

study_units.title: Dermatitis Herpetiformis and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0212.txt, pdf 212) confirms both as unmerged, contiguous subsections following Pemphigus Vulgaris: Dermatitis Herpetiformis (grouped pruritic papulovesicles, HLA-DQ2/8, celiac-disease association, dapsone/gluten-free-diet management) and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (photo-exposed skin fragility/bullae, uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency, hepatitis C/alcohol/estrogen associations). Combined as one unit given each is a short, self-contained topic with a shared vesiculobullous-adjacent presentation.

study_units.title: Drug Eruptions: Exanthematous Reaction and DRESS/DIHS
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0212.txt-0213.txt, pdf 212-213) confirms 'Drug Eruptions' with subheading 'Exanthematous', containing both the common Exanthematous Drug Reaction and the severe DRESS/DIHS syndrome. This T-child (unlike D.S06/D.S07's siblings) is not a two-column merge - its title matches the real TOC structure exactly, consistent with its LOW confidence flag reflecting OCR uncertainty rather than an actual content merge.

study_units.title: Drug-Induced Urticaria/Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0213.txt, pdf 213) confirms the 'Urticarial' drug-eruption subheading covering Drug-Induced Urticaria and Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction.

study_units.title: Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis (AGEP)
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0214.txt, pdf 214) confirms the 'Pustular' drug-eruption subheading containing AGEP (extensive sterile pustules, high fever, neutrophilia, 1-5/million rare drug reaction to aminopenicillins/cephalosporins/CCBs).

study_units.title: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (SJS/TEN)
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0214.txt, pdf 214) confirms the 'Bullous' drug-eruption subheading, whose sole content is SJS/TEN (BSA-detachment classification, SCORTEN prognosis score, high-risk drugs/HLA alleles, ICU/burn-unit management). Split into its own unit given its status as a life-threatening emergency and can't-miss diagnosis, distinct from the milder drug eruptions grouped elsewhere.

study_units.title: Fixed Drug Eruption and Photosensitivity Reaction
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0214.txt-0215.txt, pdf 214-215) confirms the 'Other' drug-eruption subheading containing Fixed Drug Eruption (recurs at the same site on re-exposure) and Photosensitivity Reaction (phototoxic vs. photoallergic).

study_units.title: Heritable Genodermatoses (Ichthyosis Vulgaris, Epidermolysis Bullosa, Oculocutaneous Albinism)
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0215.txt, pdf 215) confirms 'Heritable Disorders' as an unmerged umbrella heading with Ichthyosis Vulgaris (FLG loss-of-function, fish-scale xerosis) and Epidermolysis Bullosa (structural basement-membrane protein defects, trauma-induced blistering) as contiguous subsections; Oculocutaneous Albinism (brief entry later in the section) is grouped here as a third rare single-gene pigmentary genodermatosis. Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (SU-D-25) and Vitiligo (SU-D-26) are split out separately given their substantially greater depth and higher testability.

study_units.title: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0216.txt, pdf 216) confirms a full NF1 diagnostic-criteria subsection (>=2 of: cafe-au-lait macules, neurofibromas, axillary/inguinal freckling, optic glioma, Lisch nodules, osseous lesion, first-degree relative with NF1).

study_units.title: Vitiligo
study_units.structural_rationale: Body confirmation (clean-ocr/0217.txt, pdf 217) confirms a full Vitiligo subsection (epidemiology, autoimmune-thyroid/Addison's/T1DM association workup, Wood's lamp use, topical calcineurin inhibitor/JAK-inhibitor management).

study_units.title: Bacterial Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Impetigo, Erysipelas, Cellulitis, Folliculitis/Furuncle/Carbuncle, Skin Abscess)
source_hierarchy_path: D.S03 (Infections - umbrella; this unit covers the Bacterial Infections subsection)
study_units.structural_rationale: D.S03 ('Infections') is confirmed unmerged and matches the real TOC heading exactly (body confirmation clean-ocr/0217.txt-0219.txt, pdf 217-219): Bacterial Infections opens with Impetigo, Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (cross-ref), Table 17 Erysipelas vs. Cellulitis, Table 18 Folliculitis/Furuncle/Carbuncle, and Skin Abscess. This is the largest node in the chapter (spanning D29-D39) and is split across multiple study units by infectious subtype (SU-D-27 through SU-D-33) rather than represented as one unit, consistent with these being clinically distinct, independently testable infections.
